rubric.why: Identifies the subject of molecular biology as biological molecules.
rubric.description: States that it studies molecules found in living organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying biological molecules or molecules in living organisms as its subject.

rubric.why: Shows that the study concerns biological processes at the molecular level.
rubric.description: Explains that it studies life or biological processes at the molecular level.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for relating the study to the molecular level or molecular basis of life.

modelAnswer: Molecular biology is the branch of biology that studies biological molecules and the molecular basis of life.
It examines biological processes at the molecular level.

items.followUp: State two characteristics of a scientific theory.

rubric.why: A hypothesis must be capable of being tested.
rubric.description: States that a hypothesis is testable.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it can be tested, usually by investigation or experiment.

rubric.why: A hypothesis is a proposed explanation that may be supported or rejected by evidence.
rubric.description: Identifies a hypothesis as a tentative explanation or states that evidence may support or reject it.

modelAnswer: A hypothesis is a tentative explanation for an observation or a scientific problem.
It must be testable, and evidence may support or reject it.

items.followUp: Describe the structure of the cell membrane according to the fluid mosaic model.

rubric.why: The model describes the membrane as a phospholipid bilayer.
rubric.description: Names the phospholipid bilayer as the basic structure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying a phospholipid bilayer.

rubric.why: Proteins are distributed within or on the phospholipid bilayer, giving it a mosaic appearance; the components can move, making it fluid.
rubric.description: Describes proteins within the bilayer and/or the lateral movement that makes the membrane fluid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly describing embedded/distributed proteins or membrane fluidity.

modelAnswer: According to the fluid mosaic model, the cell membrane consists of a phospholipid bilayer.
Proteins are embedded in or attached to the bilayer, and its components can move, making it fluid and mosaic in appearance.

items.followUp: Write the taxonomic categories in order from kingdom to species.

rubric.why: A taxonomic hierarchy is an ordered arrangement of classification groups.
rubric.description: Defines the hierarchy as an arrangement of taxonomic categories or taxa.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the categories are arranged in an ordered hierarchy.

accept: species genus family order class phylum kingdom
species genus family order class division kingdom
rubric.why: The standard sequence demonstrates the hierarchical order of the categories.
rubric.description: Gives the taxonomic sequence from species up to kingdom.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct sequence, whether the plant category is called phylum or division.

modelAnswer: Taxonomic hierarchy is the orderly arrangement of organisms into taxonomic categories, from lower to higher ranks.
The main sequence is species, genus, family, order, class, phylum (or division), and kingdom.

items.followUp: What is a species? Give one example of a species.

rubric.why: Taxa are the groups or categories used in biological classification.
rubric.description: Defines taxa as groups or categories in classification.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying taxa as taxonomic groups or categories.

rubric.why: Species, genus, family, and kingdom are examples of taxonomic ranks, each of which is a taxon.
rubric.description: Gives one valid example of a taxon.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming a valid taxonomic category, such as species, genus, family, or kingdom.

modelAnswer: Taxa are the groups or categories into which organisms are classified at different taxonomic ranks.
Species is one example of a taxon.

items.followUp: What is crossing over, and during which stage of meiosis does it occur?

rubric.why: Synapsis is the pairing of homologous chromosomes.
rubric.description: Identifies the chromosomes that pair during synapsis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that homologous chromosomes pair.

rubric.why: Synapsis occurs during prophase I of meiosis.
rubric.description: Names the stage of meiosis in which synapsis occurs.

modelAnswer: Synapsis is the pairing of homologous chromosomes.
It occurs during prophase I of meiosis.

rubric.why: Mitosis is a type of cell division involving division of the nucleus.
rubric.description: Identifies mitosis as a cell or nuclear division.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is a cell or nuclear division.

accept: two daughter cells with the same chromosome number
rubric.why: Mitosis produces two genetically identical daughter cells that retain the parent cell's chromosome number.
rubric.description: States the number and/or genetic and chromosome-number outcome of mitosis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that two identical daughter cells are produced with the same chromosome number as the parent cell.

modelAnswer: Mitosis is the division of a cell in which the nucleus divides once.
It produces two genetically identical daughter cells, each with the same chromosome number as the parent cell.

items.followUp: Explain the role of photosystem II and photosystem I in non-cyclic photophosphorylation.

accept: flow of electrons from water to nadp
rubric.why: The Z scheme represents the electron pathway of non-cyclic photophosphorylation, from water towards NADP.
rubric.description: Identifies the Z scheme as the pathway of non-cyclic electron flow in photosynthesis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for connecting the scheme to non-cyclic electron flow or the transfer of electrons from water towards NADP.

rubric.why: The pathway involves excitation of electrons in photosystems II and I, which gives the diagram its characteristic Z shape.
rubric.description: Mentions the involvement of photosystems II and I or explains the characteristic Z-shaped energy pathway.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both photosystems or correctly describing the Z-shaped electron-energy pathway.

modelAnswer: The Z scheme shows the pathway of electrons during non-cyclic photophosphorylation, from water through photosystem II and photosystem I to NADP.
The changes in electron energy during this pathway form a Z-shaped pattern.
